sources.title: Armed Group Responses to Climate Shocks: A Study of FARC-EP Dissident Activities in the Colombian Amazon During an El Niño Year
sources.organization: United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR), Managing Exits from Armed Conflict project
sources.temporal_coverage: Qualitative focus groups conducted in San José del Guaviare in November 2023 and September 2024, around the 2023–2024 El Niño cycle.
sources.methodology: Two qualitative focus-group rounds in San José del Guaviare with Indigenous people, leaders, youth, authorities, military and police.
sources.limitations: One subregion; El Niño is a proxy, and concurrent political/economic changes confound attribution.

sources.title: Multiple shocks drive Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes in La Guajira and Chocó
sources.temporal_coverage: Food Security Outlook covering June 2026–January 2027; information available through 25 June 2026.
sources.methodology: FEWS NET IPC-compatible food-security outlook using national and local reports.
sources.limitations: Projection through January 2027; local conditions vary.

sources.title: MinVivienda identifica 558 municipios en riesgo y orienta acciones de preparación ante el Fenómeno El Niño
sources.organization: Ministry of Housing, City and Territory of Colombia
sources.temporal_coverage: Territorial water and sanitation risk analysis and El Niño preparedness guidance published 12 September 2026.
sources.methodology: Ministry territorial screening of potential El Niño impacts on drinking water and sanitation systems.
sources.limitations: Risk categories and recommended actions; no household-level estimates or measured service outcomes.

sources.title: Gobierno nacional alerta por altas temperaturas y aumento en probabilidad de El Niño
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, IDEAM and National Unit for Disaster Risk Management
sources.temporal_coverage: Joint national alert on May 2026 heat and rainfall conditions, fire alerts, and El Niño probability.
sources.methodology: Government alert combining IDEAM monitoring, recent observations and climate forecasts.
sources.limitations: Short-term alert and forecast; it does not confirm El Niño or attribute individual hazards to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 17–19, El Niño impacts on water, soil, crops and livelihoods
claims.paraphrase: Guaviare participants reported 2023–2024 heat and drought reduced water; some sources disappeared, while deforestation and mining further contaminated it.
claims.scenario: Participant accounts of the 2023–2024 El Niño cycle, which UNIDIR uses as a proxy for climate-change impacts.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 9–11 and 14–15, deforestation, armed-group activity and El Niño
claims.paraphrase: Dissidents exploited El Niño dryness that eased Amazon clearing for income and negotiation leverage.
claims.scenario: 2023–2024 El Niño used as a climate-change proxy.
claims.limitations: Other political/economic shifts also shaped behavior.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Report says dissidents used drought-facilitated deforestation for revenue and Total Peace leverage.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 22–24, security barriers, institutional response and local adaptations
claims.paraphrase: Security and weak state control impeded environmental operations and reforestation; community wells and Indigenous medicinal gardens aided coping.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNIDIR says armed-group control restricted access and reforestation response.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 260–262 and 320–328, La Guajira and Chocó outcomes
claims.paraphrase: In La Guajira, recurrent drought and June 2026 dry rainfall/soil conditions reduced water, pasture and rain-fed production for poor Wayuu and agropastoral households.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 260–262, 325–328 and 347, Chocó weather and conflict drivers
claims.paraphrase: In Chocó, excess rain/flood risk plus OAG insecurity and extortion restricted river transport, markets and livelihoods for poor Indigenous and Afro-Colombian riverine households.
claims.limitations: Weather, conflict and economic shocks overlap.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FEWS NET links insecurity to confinement, displacement and reduced market/livelihood access alongside weather shocks.

claims.locator: HTML paragraph 274, social-safety-net coverage and payment gaps
claims.paraphrase: Four national safety-net programs provide income support, but coverage and payment gaps limit protection against high living costs.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 121–153, municipal and regional water-risk findings
claims.paraphrase: MinVivienda screened 558 municipalities and non-municipal areas as high or very high water and sanitation risk ahead of El Niño: 111 very high, 447 high; past impacts concentrated in Andean and Caribbean regions.
claims.scenario: Possible El Niño conditions through the first quarter of 2027.
institutions: Ministry of Housing, City and Territory
claims.limitations: Territorial risk screening; no household-level exposure or outcome measure.

claims.paraphrase: The Ministry directed local governments, utilities and community water managers to monitor sources, identify alternate supplies, maintain systems and prepare tanker routes while retaining flood and landslide readiness.
claims.scenario: Preparedness guidance for possible El Niño through early 2027, including a dual drought-and-heavy-rain scenario.
claims.limitations: Circular guidance and preparedness recommendations, not completed implementation.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 14–22, regional temperature and fire-alert observations
claims.paraphrase: In May 2026, temperature anomalies reached +4.2°C in Valledupar, +4.0°C in Santa Marta, +4.4°C in Barrancabermeja and +3.3°C in Quibdó; 51.1% of active fire-alert municipalities were in the Caribbean, notably La Guajira and Magdalena.
affected_groups: residents of heat- and fire-affected municipalities
claims.limitations: May 2026 snapshot; anomalies and alert shares do not quantify household effects.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 25–42, forecast and risk-preparation guidance
claims.paraphrase: Government forecast El Niño probability rising to 82% for May–July 2026 and called for anticipatory plans for drought, water supply and wildfire, with monitoring maintained for floods and debris flows.
claims.scenario: May 2026 government forecast; a possible El Niño with below-normal rainfall and heat.
claims.limitations: Forecast at publication date; not confirmation of a later event or completed preparedness.

search_audit.query: Colombia official climate change vulnerability subnational conflict regions adaptation report government
search_audit.outcome: Full-text sources identify drought and water access risks for Wayuu/agropastoral households in La Guajira, flood and river-access risks in Chocó, and the San José del Guaviare Amazon climate-security case; government sources add named municipal and city risks.

search_audit.query: Colombia climate conflict armed groups environmental change resource conflict official UN report
search_audit.outcome: UNIDIR links El Niño drought conditions to dissident deforestation behavior in Guaviare, while FEWS NET links localized insecurity, confinement and displacement to reduced market and livelihood access in Chocó; no single-cause conflict claim is made.

search_audit.query: Colombia conflict insecurity obstruct climate adaptation public services environmental response report
search_audit.outcome: UNIDIR reports insecurity and limited state control restricted environmental-authority access and impeded government reforestation and anti-deforestation actions; this is a subregional environmental-response pathway, not evidence that all climate adaptation is obstructed nationally.

search_audit.query: Colombia climate adaptation resilience capacity municipal early warning water preparedness government report
search_audit.outcome: MinVivienda guidance directs local water actors to monitor sources and prepare alternate supply and tanker routes; MADS/IDEAM/UNGRD issued joint monitoring and anticipatory-action guidance, while Guaviare communities reported wells, medicinal gardens and reforestation efforts.

gaps: COL has no entry in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json or countries/COL baseline directory in this worktree; this extraction records primary sources without extending a prior country dossier.
UNIDIR covers one Guaviare subregion and treats El Niño as a proxy for climate-change effects; two qualitative rounds and concurrent political and economic changes limit causal attribution.
FEWS NET's 2026–2027 outlook is a forecast, and current insecurity reporting is localized; the identified pathways should not be generalized to all departments or groups.

No inspected source supports a national claim that conflict blocks all climate adaptation; the documented reverse pathway is specifically restricted environmental response and reforestation access in conflict-affected Guaviare.
